transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... my family told me to come. They keep saying I’ve been doing too much lately. I don't really know about that. 

To me, it just feels like... well, I’m the only one with enough drive to actually get things handled. We've got a move to take care of, and I'm rebuilding the new garage so it's done right... plus organizing some things down at the church. And I still have to go in and show the younger fellows at the plant how the grinding jobs actually ought to be done. 

I'm just taking care of things. That's all.
Over the past week or so, have you noticed that you need much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy the next day?
I haven't really paid much attention to it. I get enough rest to do what needs doing. Never been one to just lay around in bed all day anyway.
Would you say this level of energy and need to take charge of everything is pretty new for you over the past week or two, or is this basically how you've always been throughout your life?
Well... I suppose it's been about a month. Ever since we had to start packing up the old house. There's just been a lot to do since then.
Have you ever had a period before this—weeks or longer—where you felt unusually low, sad, or lacking energy, or a similar time of feeling extremely energetic and 'on top of the world' like this?
No... not really. I don't... I just work. Always have. I don't know about all that other stuff.
During this past month, have you had any experiences like hearing voices others can't hear, or feeling that you have special powers, a special mission, or that people are plotting against you?
No... nothing like that. I don't hear things. I just... I just have a lot of work to do right now. That's all.
In the past month, have you found yourself spending money, making big decisions, or taking risks—things like large purchases or impulsive plans—that are unusual for you?

Well... I don't know about impulsive. I just had to get things moving. I put some deposits down... for some garage work, and some new equipment. My wife wasn't too happy I didn't run it by her first, but... it needed doing. And I've been driving back and forth between the old house and the new one a lot. Trying to get jobs done at the plant, too... rushing a bit, I guess. Some folks there said I was taking chances, but... I just have to get it all done.

Have the people around you—like your family or coworkers—expressed serious concern that this pace is causing real problems, such as conflicts at work, financial strain, or safety risks, that are noticeably interfering with your daily life?

Well... yeah, I suppose they have. They... they pulled me off the floor at the plant. Said something about a safety incident. I don't know. And... my wife, she's... she won't let me handle the money right now. Or the driving. They all think I'm making a mess of the move, so... they just took it all out of my hands.

When your coworkers or wife tell you that you're overdoing it or making mistakes, do you seriously consider that they might be right, or do you feel completely certain that you're the only one who can do these jobs correctly, no matter what they say?

I don't know... I guess I just... I just thought I was doing what needed to be done. They... they think I'm messing up, but... I don't know. Maybe they're right, maybe they aren't. I just wanted to get it finished.
